item.text: [{"taxonId":140284,"summary":"An orchid genus distributed from India and the Himalayas through Southeast Asia and southern China to New Guinea and northern Australia. Most grow on trees, often becoming massive, with leathery, drought-resistant leaves and large aerial root systems; their showy, fragrant, intensely colourful flowers are prized in horticulture.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p4","s1:p13"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":140299,"summary":"An orchid genus native to Mexico, Central America, the West Indies and South America. Its small but sturdy plants mostly grow on trees in shady forests, bearing short, arching or hanging sprays of showy, fragrant flowers.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s2:p3","s2:p4"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":140477,"summary":"An orchid genus native to Asia, New Guinea and Australia. Moth orchids usually grow on trees, with coarse roots, short leafy stems, large leathery leaves and long-lasting, flat flowers on upright or hanging sprays.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p4"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":140934,"summary":"An orchid genus native to Mexico, Central America, the West Indies and northern South America, with B. caudata extending into Florida. Almost all grow on the ground or rocks in moist areas, although many also grow on trees.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":141303,"summary":"A genus of mainly stemless, evergreen bromeliads native to Brazil, southern Mexico, Central America, and northern and western South America. Its flowers have a deeply split outer cup; fibres from B. serra and B. hieronymi are economically important to the Wichí people of Argentina’s semi-arid Gran Chaco.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p3"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":141388,"summary":"A genus of small palms native to tropical and subtropical regions of the Americas. They form clumps of mainly heart- or arrow-shaped leaves, often smell strongly of anise, and hide tiny petal-free flowers inside a usually green sheath beneath the foliage.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":141488,"summary":"A genus of aquatic plants naturally distributed across tropical India, Southeast Asia and New Guinea.
